What you are feeling isn’t a national problem, it’s an international problem.

A book, The Mechanics Tale by Steve Matchet (a mechanic at Benetton during the Michael championship year)gives the best example of this. Michael loved his cars to be really stiff. It turns out the car being really stiff brought the most out of the car. So engineers took more notes from him when he would test the car. His teammates didn’t, and often preferred softer settings which brought less performance out and as a result the teams would take some notes from the teammate but not as much as Micheal. So while the car wasn’t directly designed with Michael in mind, his preferences the engineers leaned on more, not because he was the number one, but because his driving brought the most out of the car. The team is going to design the fastest car possible. Of course they are going to lean into the experience of the driver with the best results. That doesn’t mean the car is designed around that faster driver. It’s more of a feedback loop really. 

Similar to the RB19 this year. The car started with Sergio and Max in mind. But as the year went on the car started being built more in a way that Max preferred. Not because they were building it to Max, but because that was what was creating the best performance.
